They may send an authorization through a non-Jew, etc. This applies to a matter in which there is an effective kinyan, because the law of agency does not apply to a non-Jew, as Maharshal and the Shach write, and this is simple. Maharshal writes that one should not include in the authorization the phrase, "Whatever you undertake, etc.," because by doing so he makes him an agent. Yet according to what I wrote above in the name of the Rashba and Mordechai, that the arrangement is treated like a gift on condition that it be returned, the same device should work even with a non-Jew. The principal transfers ownership to him and writes, "Whatever you undertake," which merely sets an accompanying condition that the property be returned. This is simple and correct. The Shach raises a challenge to Rabbenu Tam's underlying ruling that chalipin is effective with a non-Jew. He argues that this is not implied by the Gemara. Moreover, why did the poskim labor to find other methods for transferring chametz on Pesach and the ear of a firstborn animal, rather than simply instructing that it be transferred to the non-Jew by chalipin? Rabbenu Tam's proof is from the verse, "from the money of his purchase," regarding a Hebrew servant sold to a non-Jew. The Gemara derives that such a servant is not acquired by chalipin. This implies that in other acquisitions a non-Jew can acquire by chalipin. The Shach responds that this is not a proof for two reasons. First, the verse "from the money of his purchase" does not refer only to a Hebrew servant sold to a non-Jew, but also to one sold to a Jew. Otherwise, from where would all the poskim know that a Hebrew servant is not acquired by chalipin even when sold to a Jew? Second, precisely because the Torah excluded chalipin for a Hebrew servant sold to a non-Jew, we can derive from that exclusion that all acquisitions by a non-Jew are not effected through chalipin. Rabbi Yosef similarly explains the baraita's derivation from "from the money of his purchase," that a Hebrew servant is not acquired with produce or utensils because their value is not fixed, and from this we derive the same rule for all acquisitions such as kiddushin, redemption of a firstborn son, and similar matters involving something of unfixed value. We do not say that a Hebrew servant is exceptional. So too, the exclusion of chalipin from a Hebrew servant could teach the general rule that chalipin does not effect a non-Jew's acquisitions. This is the essence of the Shach's argument against Rabbenu Tam. These arguments are not sufficient to undermine such great authorities. On the contrary, according to the Shach's latter argument, the verse "from the money of his purchase" is the source from which we would learn that chalipin does not work in a non-Jew's acquisitions. Without that verse, we would assume that chalipin does work, as the Shach himself states that the exclusion is what teaches otherwise. If so, Rabbenu Tam's ruling is actually compelled. We rule like Rav Nachman that produce does not effect chalipin. According to Rav Nachman, the Gemara expressly explains that "from the money of his purchase" is not interpreted to exclude chalipin, but rather to exclude produce and utensils that are worth less than a perutah even though they are significant, as the Gemara explains. The matter therefore returns to its original presumption, namely that chalipin is effective in acquisitions by a non-Jew, because the verse "from the money of his purchase" is used for a different derivation. The Shach's further argument, that "from the money of his purchase" must apply also to a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew, because otherwise from where would the poskim know that chalipin is ineffective even when a Hebrew servant is sold to a Jew, is likewise refuted. According to his own approach, the difficulty remains: in the Gemara's conclusion "from the money of his purchase" does not address chalipin at all, but according to Rav Nachman, who holds that produce does not effect chalipin, it is used for another derivation. We must therefore derive the rule concerning a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew from some other source. One can explain this according to Rashi's version, that "a woman does not consent to be acquired for less than a perutah." This creates a difficulty according to Levi, who holds that chalipin is performed with the utensil of the transferor. The Gemara's question would then be that a woman should be acquired by chalipin by giving the man a cloth. What difference does it make that the cloth is worth less than a perutah? On the contrary, if the purchaser takes something from her of small value and she does not consider it beneath her dignity to accept the arrangement, she certainly consents. The statement that "she does not consent to be acquired" cannot logically apply where she is the one giving the object to him. Thus according to Levi the question remains: why should she not be acquired by chalipin? We must say that Rashi holds that according to Levi, produce can serve for chalipin, and "from the money of his purchase" is then interpreted to exclude chalipin. That exclusion teaches that chalipin is absent from all acquisitions of a non-Jew. There is therefore no difficulty from learning from the field of Ephron, as Tosafot ask. But according to the Gemara's conclusion accepted by us, where produce does not effect chalipin and "from the money of his purchase" does not exclude chalipin as explained above, the Gemara properly asks that perhaps a woman should likewise be acquired by chalipin. According to our ruling that chalipin is performed with the utensil of the acquirer, the Gemara properly answers that a woman does not consent to be acquired for less than a perutah. This is precise. Admittedly, Tosafot in Kiddushin 3a, beginning "And a woman," do not appear to say exactly what I have written, that according to the initial understanding that "from the money of his purchase" excludes chalipin, we would say that all acquisitions of a non-Jew lack chalipin, as the Shach suggests. Nevertheless, Rabbenu Tam's ruling remains correct. Apart from the fact that Tosafot's wording does not expressly establish the Shach's reading, if that were Tosafot's intention their question would be difficult. Tosafot ask why a verse is needed to exclude chalipin for a Hebrew servant when one can learn from a woman that chalipin is ineffective, and if it does not work for a Jew it certainly should not work for a non-Jew, as the Maharsha explains. According to the Shach's reading, the verse is needed to exclude chalipin from all acquisitions of a non-Jew, not merely the acquisition of a Hebrew servant. This is not a decisive difficulty, because Tosafot later say that it would be strained for the Torah to write an exclusion in the section of a Hebrew servant solely to teach rules concerning other acquisitions when it is unnecessary for the servant himself. The wording of Tosafot, however, does not support the Shach's reading at all. Rather, it appears that Tosafot understand the verse to apply specifically to a Hebrew servant. One cannot say that it establishes a rule for all acquisitions of a non-Jew, because the verse does not apply only to a Hebrew servant sold to a non-Jew. It also addresses one sold to a Jew. Yet chalipin plainly works for a Jew in other types of acquisition, so how could the rule for a Hebrew servant serve as a source for all acquisitions? If one asks that if the verse also applies to a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew, how can Rabbenu Tam prove from the need to exclude chalipin that chalipin otherwise works for a non-Jew? Perhaps the exclusion is needed only for the Jewish purchaser, as the Shach argues. The answer is that if the exclusion had no relevance at all to a non-Jew and were needed only for a Jew, the Torah would not have placed it in the section concerning a servant sold to a non-Jew. Even if the verse can also be applied to a sale to a Jew, its natural location would have been in the section of a servant sold to a Jew. Its placement here demonstrates that the exclusion is also needed regarding a non-Jew, meaning that outside the special law of a Hebrew servant chalipin can be effective for him. We also cannot derive from this special exclusion that chalipin never works for a non-Jew, because the verse demonstrably addresses a Jewish purchaser too, and chalipin certainly works for Jews in other matters. Indeed, it seems that this itself is Tosafot's proof. The Mishnah states that a Hebrew servant is acquired by money and a document, and does not list chalipin. This implies, as is evident throughout the sugya, that a Hebrew servant is not acquired by chalipin even when sold to a Jew. The Shach asks from where this is known. If it came from some entirely different source, then according to the opinion that "from the money of his purchase" excludes chalipin, that exclusion would be unnecessary regarding a Jewish purchaser, because chalipin is already ineffective there, and all the more so should it be ineffective for a non-Jew. One cannot answer that the verse comes merely to teach that all acquisitions of a non-Jew do not work through chalipin. It is strained to say that the Torah placed an exclusion in the law of a Hebrew servant where it is wholly unnecessary, only for the sake of other acquisitions. More fundamentally, one cannot derive other acquisitions from a Hebrew servant, for we see that even for a Jew chalipin works in other matters and nevertheless does not acquire a Hebrew servant. We must therefore say that there is no independent exclusion from chalipin for a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew. Rather, his law is learned by a binyan av or other indication from the servant sold to a non-Jew, as the language of Tosafot itself indicates. This works only if chalipin is generally effective in other acquisitions of a non-Jew and is excluded specifically for a Hebrew servant. We can then extend that servant-specific rule to a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew. But if a non-Jew can never acquire anything by chalipin, how could we infer from that fact that a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew is not acquired by chalipin? In the non-Jew's case there would be no distinction at all between acquiring a Hebrew servant and acquiring any other property, while for a Jew chalipin works generally. Tosafot are therefore compelled to hold that chalipin does work for a non-Jew in other acquisitions and is excluded only for a Hebrew servant, allowing us to derive the law of a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew from it. That Tosafot understand "from the money of his purchase" as applying specifically to a Hebrew servant sold to a non-Jew, and not to one sold to a Jew, is also compelled by Tosafot in Bava Batra 54b, beginning "A non-Jew, from the time the money reaches him." They write: "Furthermore, it is taught there, 'from the money of his purchase,' he is acquired with money but not with produce and utensils, meaning chalipin. This implies that similarly he is not acquired by a document, for even all forms of money-equivalent would have been excluded from 'money' had Scripture not written 'he shall give.' But elsewhere this is not so." If the verse also governed a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew, how could a document be excluded? A Hebrew servant sold to a Jew is expressly acquired by a document. We must therefore say that this derivation concerns only one sold to a non-Jew. The fact that chalipin does not work for one sold to a Jew is learned from the one sold to a non-Jew. A document is different, because it cannot be learned across that comparison. The law of a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew is linked to a Hebrew maidservant, who in turn is linked to a woman, and a document is effective there. This also resolves another apparent difficulty. If Tosafot infer from the exclusion of chalipin for a Hebrew servant acquired by a non-Jew that chalipin generally exists for a non-Jew, why not similarly infer from the exclusion of a document that documents generally work for a non-Jew? Yet in that same passage Tosafot conclude that documents are not an acquisition method for a non-Jew even regarding land, because the verse concerning a deed of acquisition is written with respect to Jews. One might answer that Tosafot's proof is not from the verse itself but from the wording of the baraita. The baraita says, "from the money of his purchase, not with produce and utensils," which specifically denotes chalipin. Since the verse itself excludes every non-cash method, including a document, why did the baraita select produce and utensils? It could be because chalipin is generally available to non-Jews and is therefore a greater novelty to exclude for a Hebrew servant, whereas a document never works for them. But this explanation is strained and not especially indicated by Tosafot's wording. According to what I wrote, the matter is simple. Tosafot's entire proof is that if chalipin did not work for a non-Jew in other acquisitions, we could not derive from his inability to acquire a Hebrew servant by chalipin that a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew is likewise not acquired by chalipin. With a document, however, we indeed say that it does not work for a non-Jew in other acquisitions, because a Hebrew servant sold to a Jew is independently acquired by a document. Everything fits well. Tosafot ask why "from the money of his purchase" is needed to exclude chalipin when even for a Jew chalipin does not acquire a Hebrew servant by the comparison to a woman. They do not answer that it excludes documents, which do work for a Jewish purchaser of a Hebrew servant but not for a non-Jew. It is possible that their question is directed at the wording of the baraita: why did it formulate the exclusion as produce and utensils, meaning chalipin, a method already ineffective even for a Jew? It should instead have identified the novelty of a document, which is effective for a Jewish purchaser of a Hebrew servant but not for a non-Jew. The Gemara similarly asks according to the opinion that produce does not effect chalipin why the verse is needed, rather than answering that it excludes a document. Evidently the difficulty is with the baraita's formulation. In any event, there is no real difficulty, because a document is nowhere established as a mode of acquisition for a non-Jew and therefore needs no special verse to exclude it. Documents are mentioned by Scripture specifically among Jews, as Tosafot write. There is thus no need to force the explanation that Tosafot in Bava Batra wrote according to the Rashbam's initial view, that a non-Jew withdraws because all his acquisitions are by money, while under that initial view a document might have worked for him in a gift or another case where money has no role, so that a Hebrew servant required a special exclusion from "from the money of his purchase." According to Tosafot's ultimate conclusion that a document is never an acquisition mode for a non-Jew, they would then hold that the verse excludes only chalipin, which is why the Kiddushin passage does not mention exclusion of a document. According to what I have written, no such forced distinction is necessary. The Shach's answer to Tosafot's other question is, however, good. Tosafot ask how we could say that chalipin acquires a woman through the gezeirah shavah of "taking" from the field of Ephron if chalipin itself did not acquire Ephron's field. The Shach answers that the derivation is not literally from Ephron's field, but rather the Torah compares the acquisition of a woman to acquisition of a field in general. The Rashba in his chiddushim to Kiddushin explicitly writes this answer. Nevertheless, the Rashba concludes that Rabbenu Tam answered in Tosafot that chalipin does apply to a non-Jew; see there. Thus the Rashba concedes Rabbenu Tam's ruling. Indeed, Rabbenu Tam's explanation is more straightforward, because according to the Shach and Rashba one must still explain how the Gemara knew to ask that a woman should be acquired by chalipin. Perhaps the gezeirah shavah specifically compares her to Ephron's field, where chalipin did not work, rather than to fields in general. Yet I have a further difficulty. If Tosafot hold that we learn literally from the field of Ephron and that chalipin was applicable there, why did Tosafot labor, according to Rashi's interpretation, to ask that we should also derive that a document acquires a woman, making the verse "she shall leave and become" unnecessary? A document does not apply to Ephron's field, as Tosafot in Bava Batra expressly write and as cited above. How then can a document be derived? According to the Rashba's and Shach's understanding, Tosafot's question is clear, because we compare the acquisition of a woman to acquisition of a field generally, and a document does acquire fields. One must say that in truth the question from documents is not so strong. How could we derive that a document of kiddushin works from the acquisition of a field? In a field the seller gives the document to the purchaser, whereas in kiddushin the man, who is the acquirer, gives the document to the woman, who is acquired. See Kiddushin 9a, where the Gemara concludes that these are independent halachot, and see Tosafot there. We must therefore say that Tosafot's main question was from chazakah, and they mentioned a document only incidentally with the flow of language. Still, the matter requires study. I later saw in Atzmot Yosef that he leaves these two questions unresolved. Regarding the second question he strengthens it further from Tosafot's explicit later statement that we cannot derive a document for kiddushin by a kal vachomer from a Hebrew maidservant, because there the father writes the document whereas here the husband writes it. The second question can actually be answered. If we were seeking to derive by kal vachomer that a document should acquire a woman because it acquires a maidservant, Tosafot properly object that in the maidservant case the father writes the document. How can one infer that a document written by the husband should work? Here, by contrast, Scripture writes "when a man takes," and with respect to a field Scripture also uses the language of taking. Through the gezeirah shavah we learn that all acquisition methods included in the "taking" of a field are included in the "taking" of a woman. If the word "taking" in the field context includes a document, then "when a man takes" likewise includes a document. Once the meaning of "taking" has been established to include a document, we return to the immediate context of the verse, which says "when a man takes," meaning that he is the one who gives it, as the Gemara later explains. We are not deriving the mechanics of one case from the other, only the meaning of the word "taking." There it means money and a document, and here too "when he takes" means money and a document. We then apply the local context of each verse. This is precise. The first question, however, still appears difficult. The Maharsha already asks Tosafot's question why a separate verse is needed for a document if it can be learned from Ephron's field, since the Gemara ultimately says that a woman does not consent to be acquired for less than a perutah. It therefore appears that Tosafot's questions operate as alternatives: either the first question or the second. We asked above that according to Tosafot in Bava Batra, even a document is excluded by "from the money of his purchase." If so, just as Rabbenu Tam infers from the special exclusion of chalipin that chalipin must generally be effective in acquisitions of a non-Jew, we could infer from exclusion of a document that a document too generally works for a non-Jew. In truth there is no difficulty. The verse must exclude from a Hebrew servant sold to a non-Jew some acquisition method that works in other acquisitions of a non-Jew, otherwise the exclusion would be unnecessary. But it is enough that one such method exists. Thus either the verse excludes a document because documents generally work for a non-Jew, or it excludes chalipin because chalipin generally works for him. Rabbenu Tam finds it more reasonable that the verse excludes chalipin rather than a document, because he regards it as certain that a document never works for a non-Jew. The verse concerning a deed of acquisition is written with respect to Jews. The sugya in which a non-Jew's property becomes like ownerless property after payment likewise supports this, as Tosafot write in Kiddushin 14b, beginning "Since." Regarding Tosafot's question on Rashi, that if the only reason chalipin does not work for kiddushin is that a woman does not consent to be acquired for less than a perutah, why should that depend on her will, similar to the Gemara's later question regarding Beit Shammai, one can say that Rashi agrees with the force of this question. Rashi, however, holds that chalipin does not operate in acquisitions of a non-Jew, as appears from Tosafot's understanding of Rashi. The Gemara's question, "Perhaps so too," is therefore answered in the manner of the Rashba and Shach, namely that perhaps the gezeirah shavah compares a woman's acquisition to fields generally rather than to Ephron's specific field. Yet how do we know this? Particularly to rule leniently that a woman is not betrothed by chalipin at all and requires no get, perhaps the gezeirah shavah is from Ephron specifically and would not include chalipin. The Gemara answers that because both interpretive possibilities exist, and there is an independent reason that chalipin should not work, namely that a woman does not consent to be acquired for less than a perutah, it is more reasonable to interpret the gezeirah shavah from Ephron himself, where chalipin was absent, rather than from fields generally so as to create an acquisition by chalipin against that independent rationale. This is a satisfactory resolution. Tosafot's question does not arise, because the statement that a woman does not consent is not itself overriding an otherwise established acquisition. It merely determines which of two possible readings of the gezeirah shavah is preferable. According to this, Rashi holds that chalipin is ineffective for a non-Jew. We must then say that a document does work for a non-Jew, because otherwise what purpose would "from the money of his purchase" serve? It could not be needed to exclude chalipin, since chalipin is already absent from every acquisition by a non-Jew. Tosafot therefore properly ask, on this interpretation, why a separate verse is needed to establish acquisition of a woman by document. It should be learned from Ephron, because according to this approach a document necessarily can be used in a non-Jew's acquisition. This also answers the Maharsha's objection. We are presently assuming that the statement "a woman does not consent to be acquired for less than a perutah" serves only to choose the correct direction of the gezeirah shavah. If the gezeirah shavah itself clearly established an acquisition, her lack of subjective consent would not negate the Torah's acquisition mechanism. This is precise. In my chiddushim I discuss at length that if we learned literally from Ephron, even less than a perutah might suffice, because a descendant of Noach is liable for theft of less than a perutah, so for him such an amount constitutes money and could acquire a field. This is not the place for that discussion.
However from all these discussions it appears that Rabbenu Tam did not build his ruling that chalipin works for a non-Jew upon this secondary resolution of Tosafot's question. His principal proof is the verse "from the money of his purchase," and, as we have clarified, that is a complete proof without a sufficient refutation. Rashi and Rashbam, however, interpret the statement in Kiddushin 14b that "all of a non-Jew's acquisitions are with money" to mean all of his acquisitions generally, implying that he has no acquisition by chalipin, since all his acquisitions are by money. I already used this to resolve Rashi against Tosafot's question. Rabbenu Tam follows his own view in Tosafot there, that "all his acquisitions are with money" does not refer to every type of property, but only to a Hebrew servant, concerning whom all his acquisition is by money. It therefore remains entirely consistent that in other matters even chalipin works. See the Rashba's chiddushim to Kiddushin, who asks against Rashi's explanation that every acquisition of a non-Jew is by money from the fact that chazakah also exists; see there. This demonstrates that Rashi understands "all his acquisitions are with money" as excluding all other acquisition methods. The Shach's objection from the methods used to transfer chametz on Pesach and the ear of a firstborn animal is now answered. In monetary matters, and especially in the technical context of authorization, we rely on Rabbenu Tam because his reasoning is compelling and many commentators agree with his reading that the statement does not mean every acquisition by a non-Jew is limited to money. But regarding prohibitions, the poskim in those areas labor to satisfy all opinions, as is evident from their discussions. They therefore also took into account Rashi and Rashbam and did not wish to rely solely on Rabbenu Tam. It also appears from here that acquisition by way of land, agav karka, does not work for a non-Jew. Otherwise why did Rabbenu Tam not advise, for an authorization through a non-Jew, that the claim be transferred agav land? That is a standard mode of transfer used in authorizations and is more effective for several matters for which a sudar is ineffective. Likewise, regarding chametz and firstborn animals, why did the authorities not advise transfer agav land? Evidently it is ineffective. Indeed, we do not find anywhere that agav karka works for a non-Jew. Tosafot write that a document does not work for them because the verse concerning a deed of acquisition is written regarding Jews. Similarly, the verse "and he gave them gifts," from which agav is derived, is written concerning Yehoshafat. Chalipin is different. Without specific proof we would indeed have assumed that it works for a non-Jew, and the verse "this was formerly the custom in Israel" does not refute Rabbenu Tam, despite Maharshal's formulation as though Rabbenu Tam contradicted Scripture. The verse means that this was the recognized custom among Israel. Non-Jews did not customarily use it because they did not know these civil laws. Therefore Scripture says, "this was formerly the custom in Israel," rather than simply, "this applies in Israel." According to this I initially thought there was an additional proof for Rabbenu Tam. The Shitah Mekubetzet cites a question in the chapter HaZahav: according to the opinion that movable property is not acquired by meshichah, how can a gift of movable property ever be acquired? Tosafot answer, as cited there and in Avodah Zarah, that a gift itself is not enough to create acquisition and the issue is undisputed. The Ramban answers that other acquisition methods exist, namely kinyan sudar, agav karka, and chatzer. The Ramban's words seem correct, for why should there be a distinction between gift and sale? Otherwise, why were all the poskim so concerned about transferring the ear of a firstborn animal without relying on meshichah? According to Rashi, who holds that meshichah does not acquire for a non-Jew, one could simply give him the ear as a gift. Meshichah would then work according to all views. The Jew does not need payment for it. According to this, however, a difficulty arises for Reish Lakish, who holds that a non-Jew acquires specifically with money. How can a non-Jew ever acquire a gift? Agav karka is unavailable to him, as explained above. Chatzer is likewise unavailable according to Reish Lakish, because Reish Lakish says in Bava Metzia 10b that a minor girl has no acquisition through chatzer, since chatzer is derived from agency and a minor lacks agency. The same should apply to a non-Jew, who likewise has no law of agency. By what method can he acquire a gift? We must therefore say, in accordance with Rabbenu Tam, that a non-Jew can acquire by chalipin. The conclusion is nearly compelled. It is therefore simple that one should not depart from Rabbenu Tam's ruling, and who would dare rule against him. Maharshal's extra formulation that Rabbenu Tam is a lone opinion was unnecessary, for Tosafot, the Rashba as cited above, the Mordechai, other authorities, the Tur, and the Shulchan Aruch all support his position.

mechaber.he: יכול אדם להרשות נשים ועבדים ויש מי שאומר אבל לא את עבדו שאין קנין לעבד ע"י רבו שהרי גופו קנוי לו וידו כידו נמצא שאינו אלא שלוחו ויכול הנתבע לומר לאו בעל דברים דידי את אבל יכול להרשות את אשתו שהרי אם נתן לה מתנה קנתה ואין הבעל אוכל פירות נמצא כשכתב לה זכי לנפשך אין הנתבע יכול לומר לאו בעל דברים דידי את:
mechaber.en: A man can afford women and servants and there is no one who says but you don't work that can't be processed by his body, because his body is bought by him and said that his friend is nothing but rejected and can be told to him that he has nothing to do with, but can afford his wife, because if he has given her a gift, and no fruit food is found when he wrote to her, the defendant cannot say no words

baer_hetev.he: פירות. אבל אם הי' הבעל אוכל פירות אפשר דלא הי' יכול לשלוח הרשא' ע"י אשתו אע"פ שהגוף ישאר לה ול"ד למ"ש הט"ו בסי' קכ"ב ס"ח דהאיש יוכל לדון עם המחזיק בנכסי אשתו אף בלי הרשאה כשיש בו פירות מתוך שיכול לדון על הפירות דשאני הכא דלא נראה הנאתה ממנו אף כשתוציא שהרי הבעל אוכל פירות וגם גוף השדה אם תמות היא קודם ישאר ביד בעלה ומקור דין זה נתבאר בא"ע סימן פ"ה ע"ש כ"כ הסמ"ע וכ' הש"ך דנראה מדבריו דה"ה אם נתן מתחל' מתנה לאשתו קרקע ע"מ שיאכל הפירות א"י לדון עמו על הפירות וכן אם הוא בענין שהקרקע היא של בעל כל ימי חייו והפירות של אשתו א"י לדון עמו. ולע"ד זה אינו דאדרבה יותר מסתבר שיוכל לדון כשהקרקע שלו משיכול לדון כשהפירות שלו והכא שאני דאם הי' אוכל פירות נמצא לא היתה יכולה לדון בהרשא' זו על הפירות דהא לא שייך לומר מתוך שיכולה לדון על הקרקע כו' דהא בקרקע גופה עדיין אין לה שום זכות והיאך נאמר בה מתוך משא"כ בסימן קכ"ב שהפירו' כבר הם שלו ושייך לומר מתוך כו' עכ"ל:
baer_hetev.en:
fruits. But if the husband eats fruit, he can send permissions by his wife, he will be able to discuss his wife’s possessions with no permission to discuss the fruits of his or her husband’s household, and he will be able to speak to him
The life and fruit of his wife A. will be discussed with him. And this is not more Darwinian, it turns out that he could discuss when his soil is able to discuss his fruits and the depress that I am a fruitful food found could not have discussed this authorization for the fruits of Dea, and that he could discuss the ground as a dea in the land of his body still has no right, and that it is said in it from a sign that he has already said

beer_hagolah.he:
שם סימן ד' כ"כ בעה"ת בשם ת' גאון והביא ראיה מברייתא אין ממנין אפוטרופוס נשים וכו' ואם מינן אביהם הרשות בידו גיטין נ"ב ע"א
טור שם לאפוקי ממ"ש המרדכי פרק מרובה דיכול להרשות את עבדו
(פי' וכל הרשאה שאינו מקנה לו הממון של תביעה וכותב לו דון ואפיק לנפשך לאו הרשאה היא כמ"ש בסימן קכ"ב סמ"ע)
beer_hagolah.en:
There, siman 4. Baal HaTerumot writes so in the name of a responsum of a Gaon and brings proof from the baraita, "Women are not appointed as guardians," etc.; but if their father appointed one, he has the authority to do so, Gittin 52a.
Tur there, excluding Mordechai's ruling in Merubah that one may authorize his slave.
Meaning, any authorization in which the principal does not transfer ownership of the claim to the agent and write, "Litigate and recover for yourself," is not a valid authorization, as Sema writes in siman 122.

beur_hagra.he:
אבל לא את כו'. כמ"ש בגטין כ"ג ב' נראין דברים שהעבד כו' ובב"מ צ"ט א' י"ד כו':
אבל יכול כו'. כמ"ש בנדרים פ"ח ב' אע"ג דאר"מ כו' וער"ן שם ד"ה מודה ר"מ כו' ואע"ג דלא קיימא האי תירוצא שם משום דאינו נותן לה ממש וכמ"ש הר"ן שם וע"ש ד"ה אלא אמר רב אשי וכ"ש לדידן דקי"ל דלא כתי' דרב אשי ועמ"ש בש"ע א"ח סי' שס"ו:
שהרי כו'. ב"ב נ"א ב' ע"ש:
beur_hagra.en:
But not you, etc. Gittin 23b and Bava Metzia 99 teach that a person cannot act as agent where his legal status prevents the act from applying through him.
But he may, etc. Nedarim 88b recognizes a transfer made for another's benefit even under restrictions on direct acquisition. Although that particular explanation is rejected there because the recipient does not receive the property outright, it supports the present rule, all the more according to the law we follow. See citation 366.
For, etc. This follows Bava Batra 51b.

chelkat_mechokek.he: ואין לגרש בלילה. לא קאי אכתיבת הגט וחתימתו דהא ודאי מותר לכתוב ולחתום הגט בלילה כמו שיתבאר בסימן קכ"ז אלא אנתינת הגט קאי וכתב הב"י לקמן סימן קל"ו דשמע הטעם משום דנתינת הגט הוי כמו דין ואין דנין בלילה והב"י השיג ע"ז וכמו שאעתיק לשונו בסמוך:
chelkat_mechokek.en: And one should not divorce at night. This does not refer to writing or signing the get, for it is certainly permitted to write and sign a get at night, as will be explained in siman 127. Rather, it refers to delivery of the get. Beit Yosef writes below in siman 136 that he heard the reason to be that delivery of a get resembles adjudication, and courts do not adjudicate at night. Beit Yosef rejects this reason, as I will cite shortly.

meirat_einayim.he:
שאין קנין לעבד. פי' וכל הרשאה שאינו מקנה לו הממון של תביע' וכותב לו דון ואפיק לנפשך לאו הרשא' הוא כמ"ש בסי' קכ"ב:
ויכול הנתבע לומר לאו בעל דברים דידי את. פי' לענין זה שאינו יכול לכופו שיתננו לו שהרי יש לו חששא שמא בטלה השליחות או "שמת ויאנסו המעות מיד השליח ויצטרך לחזור ולשלם כיון שאין להרשא' זה דין הרשאה וכמ"ש הט"ו ר"ס קכ"ב אבל עכ"פ לא גרע "משליח שעשאו בעדים וכמ"ש בס"א מסי' זה ובסי' קכ"ב ס"ד:
ואין הבעל אוכל פירות. אבל אם היה הבעל אוכל פירות אפשר דלא היה יכול לשלוח הרשאה ע"י אע"פ שהגוף ישאר לה ול"ד לאיש שיכול לדון עם אחר המחזיק בנכסי אשתו אפי' בלי הרשא' כשיש בו פירות מתוך שיכול לדון על הפירות וכמ"ש הט"ו בסי' קכ"ב ס"ח דשאני הכא דלא נראה הנאת' ממנו אף כשתוציא שהרי הבעל אוכל פירות ומי יודע שמא תמות היא קודם וישאר גם גוף השד' ביד בעל' ועמ"ש עוד בפריש' מזה. ומקור דין זה נתבאר בא"ע סימן פ"ה עיין שם:
meirat_einayim.en:
A slave has no independent acquisition. Therefore an authorization that does not transfer the subject of the claim to the representative and state, "Litigate and recover for yourself," is not a valid authorization, as explained in siman 122.
The defendant can say, "You are not my litigant." Meaning he cannot compel the defendant to pay him, because there remains a concern that the agency may have been revoked or the principal died, in which case the money could be taken from the agent by force and the defendant might have to pay again. Since this authorization lacks the legal status of a complete authorization, the concern remains. Nevertheless, it is no worse than an ordinary agent appointed before witnesses, as explained earlier.
The husband does not consume the fruits. If the husband were entitled to the fruits, perhaps the wife could not issue an authorization even though the principal ownership remains hers. This is unlike the rule that a husband can litigate regarding property held by another when he has rights to the fruits, even without authorization, because there his own present benefit gives him standing. Here, if the husband consumes the fruits, the wife's practical benefit from recovery is not apparent; she may die first and even the principal of the field will ultimately remain with the husband. The source of this law is explained in Even HaEzer siman 85.

siftei_kohen.he:
[" אבל לא את עבדו כו'. וכ\"פ מהרש\"ל שם סי' י\"ג ונראה דאף דקי\"ל דיכול להרשות אפי' בדבר שא\"י להקנות כמו שנתבאר בר\"ס זה היינו משום דכשיבא המעות לידו יקנהו משא\"כ עבדו שאפילו יגיע לידו יהיה של רבו דמה שקנה עבד קנה רבו ונמצא דלא שייך ביה זיל דון ואפיק לנפשך. וכתב הסמ\"ע ומ\"מ אם הנתבע נתן לו פטור דלא גרע משליח שעשאו בעדים ופשוט הוא:"]
[" ויכול הנתבע לומר כו'. ע\"ל סי' קכ\"ב ס\"ק י\"ז:"]
[" ואין הבעל אוכל פירות. אבל אם היה הבעל אוכל פירות אפשר דלא הי' יכול לשלוח הרשאה על ידה אע\"פ שהגוף ישאר לה ול\"ד לבעל שיכול לדון עם אחר המחזיק בנכסי אשתו אפילו בלא הרשאה כשיש בו פירות מתוך שיכול לדון על הפירות וכמ\"ש הטור בסי' קכ\"ב ס\"ח דשאני הכא דלא נראה הנאתה ממנו אף כשתוציא שהרי הבעל אוכל פירות ומי יודע שמא תמות היא קודם וישאר גם גוף השדה ביד בעלה עכ\"ל סמ\"ע ונראה מדבריו דה\"ה אם נתן מתחל' במתנה לאשתו הקרקע ע\"מ שיאכל הפירות א\"י לדון עמו על הפירות וכן אם הוא בענין שהקרקע הוא של בעל כל ימי חייו והפירות של אשתו א\"י לדון עמו ולפע\"ד זה אינו דאדרב' יותר מסתבר שיכול לדון כשהקרקע שלו משיכול לדון כשהפירות שלו והא דאצרכינן הכא למימר קנת' ואין הבעל אוכל פירות כו' היינו משום שאם היה אוכל פירות נמצא לא הית' יכול' לדון בהרשאה זו על הפירות דהא לא שייך לו' מתוך שיכולה לדון על הקרקע יכולה לדון על הפירות דהא בקרקע גופא עדיין אין לה שום זכות והאיך נאמר בה מתוך כו' משא\"כ לעיל סי' קכ\"ב שהפירות כבר שלו ושייך לו' מתוך כו' ודוק:"]
siftei_kohen.en:
But not his slave. Maharshal rules likewise. Although authorization may generally be given even concerning something that cannot be transferred, that is because the agent will acquire the money when it reaches him. A slave, however, acquires everything for his master, so even when the money reaches him it remains the master's. The formula “go litigate and recover for yourself” therefore cannot apply. Sema adds that if the defendant nevertheless pays the slave, the defendant is exempt, since the slave is no worse than an agent appointed before witnesses.
The defendant may say. See above, siman 122, seif katan 17.
There is no fruit. But if the husband had fruit food, he could send permission to his wife’s possessions, and he would be able to speak to the man who holds his wife’s possessions without permission, even if he had any fruit, and he would be able to discuss the fruit, and he would be able to speak to his wife The life and fruits of his wife A. to discuss with him and the abundance of this is not more likely to be discussed when his land is able to discuss his fruit and his follicles, and that the husband has not eaten any fruit as he is, and that he has no reason to speak of the fruit of the earth

urim_vetumim_tumim.he: ובלבד שיזהר מלכתוב וכו' עיין הטעם בסמ"ע ס"ק כ"א וכך כתב המהרש"א להדיא בשם תוספות ישנים עיין שם. והנה הרב הש"ך בס"ק ל"א הביא דעת מהרשד"ם דגוי לישראל אף ר"ת מודה דא"י להרשות ודבריו בלתי נכונים דודאי בענין אשר לא טוב עושה בעמו ודאי יפה דיבר מהיכי תיתי להוציא מיד ישראל ולתתן לגוי אם לא דיש ח"ה בדבר וכדומה לבל יעלילו עלינו בגולה כי נחנו מסייעים לעושים עול וממון של גוי הפקר אצלנו בעו"ה היא המעוררת מדנים ומטלת שנאה עלינו בין אומ' וגורם רעות רבות לישראל ההולכים לתומם תומת ישרים ולכך נהגו בזמנינו לפעמים היתר בזה ולא מיחו בידם חכמי הדור. אבל לדינא בקנין דבריו אינו מובנים דפשוט דהיכי דמהני קנין בגוי הקונה מישראל ה"ה בישראל הקונה מגוי דמ"ש בקניני' והא תי' התוס' דבגוי מהני חליפין על שדה עפרון למילף מיניה קדושי אשה והתם גוי הקנה לישראל הוה וכן רשב"ם בב"ב גבי נכסי גוים דכתב דגוי מסתלק בזוזי דכל קנינו אינו אלא בכסף וזהו גבי קנין הגוי לנפשו ובב"ב איירי דהגוי יקנה לישראל. ואיך ניליף זה מזה אלא ודאי דכל קנינים בכזה שוים בדינים וכן נראה בכמה דוכתי מתוס' דהשוו דינם ואדרבא יותר אלים וטוב להפקיע נכסי גוי משנפקיע נכסי ישראל ולכן אין לדבריו שרש ועיקר בש"ם ובפוסקים וברור:
urim_vetumim_tumim.en: Provided that he is careful not to write, etc. See the reason in Sema seif katan 21, and Maharshal explicitly writes the same in the name of the old Tosafot; see there. The Shach in seif katan 31 cites Maharshadam as holding that where a non-Jew gives authorization against a Jew, even Rabbenu Tam agrees that the authorization cannot be used. His words are incorrect as a matter of law. Certainly, with respect to the prohibition of doing what is improper toward one's fellow, Maharshadam spoke well. Why should one assist in extracting money from a Jew and giving it to a non-Jew, unless there is concern of desecration of Hashem's name or the like, so that accusations not be raised against us in exile that we assist wrongdoing and regard a non-Jew's money as ownerless? Unfortunately, such conduct provokes strife and hatred against us among the nations and causes much harm to Jews who walk innocently and uprightly. Therefore in our times people have at times acted leniently in such situations, and the sages of the generation did not protest. But regarding the law of acquisition itself, Maharshadam's words are not understandable. Wherever a kinyan is effective when a non-Jew acquires from a Jew, the same kinyan is effective when a Jew acquires from a non-Jew. Why should the laws of acquisition differ in that respect? Tosafot explain that chalipin worked in the field of Ephron, so that kiddushin can be derived from it, and there the non-Jew transferred property to a Jew. Likewise the Rashbam in Bava Batra, regarding property of non-Jews, writes that the non-Jew withdraws from the property upon receiving money because all of his acquisition is with money. There he is discussing a non-Jew transferring to a Jew. How could these rules be learned from one another unless the acquisition laws are symmetrical in this respect? Tosafot likewise equate the two directions in many places. If anything, it is more readily accepted that the property of a non-Jew can be removed from his possession than that Jewish property can be removed from a Jew. Maharshadam's distinction therefore has no basis in Shas or poskim. This is clear.

mechaber.he: יכולים לשלוח הרשאה ביד עכו"ם ובלבד שיזהר מלכתוב בה וקנינא מיניה דאין שליחות וזכייה לעכו"ם אלא יכתוב וקנה העכו"ם:
mechaber.en: It is possible to send permissions in the hands of the psalmist, so that it is written in it, and that it is not a mission to receive it, but rather to write and buy it:

baer_hetev.he:
עובד כוכבים. כתב הסמ"ע בשם הטור דילפינן מקרא דעובד כוכבים קונה בחליפין מש"ה כשהעובד כוכבים נותן סודרו לישראל המרשה ואוחז בו ומקנה לו חליפיו חובו או פקדונו שיש לו ביד אחר זכה העובד כוכבים בו כדין מורשה ומהני מיהו זהו דוקא כשהעכו"ם עצמו מוסר החליפין לישראל אבל אין העדים יכולים לקנות עבורו מהמרש' כדרך שאר קנינים דהעדים נותנין סודר שלהם להמקנ' והם זוכים להקונה עבורו דזכין לאדם שלא בפניו וכמ"ש הטור בסי' קצ"ה שכן הי' רוב הקנינים גם בזמניהם כו' ואז כותבין העדים קנינו מפלו' המקנה לפלו' הזוכה במנא דכשר כו' וזהו שסיים הטור דבהקנה על ידו לעובד כוכבים אין כותבין בהרשא' וקנינא כו' דהא אין העדים נעשים שלוחים לעכו"ם לזכות על ידו אלא יכתבו וקנה העכו"ם ר"ל שעשה העובד כוכבים קנין חליפין בעצמו עכ"ל והש"ך כתב דמהרש"ל חולק ע"ז והעל' דבהלוא' ושאר דברים שאינן נקנין בחליפין פשיטא שאין הרשא' מועיל לעובד כוכבים דכיון דבזה אין המורש' רק בתורת שליחות ואין שליחות לעובד כוכבים אבל בקרקע ופקדון יכול להקנות לעובד כוכבים בק"ס שמועיל חליפין לעובד כוכבים אבל לא יכתוב כל מה דמתעני כו' שהוא לשון שליחות עכ"ד וכה"ג כתב בתשובת מהרשד"ם סי' נ"ט ע"ש ובזה הי' נרא' לומר דגם דעת ר"ת כן כו' רק מדברי המחבר משמע דהרשא' מועיל לעובד כוכבים בכל ענין אך לבי מהסס בעיקר הדין שסובר ר"ת דחליפין מועיל לעובד כוכבים כו' ע"ש שהאריך בראיות וכתב דכן מצא בתשובת מהר"מ מינץ סימן ה' שכתב בפשיטות דלא מצינו חליפין לעובד כוכבים גם בתשו' מהרשד"ם סימן נ"ט כתב שנ"ל דסברת ר"ת דעת יחיד היא כו' אך שלא כתב טעם לדבר וע"ש:
שליחות. ובתשו' רש"ך ס"ב סי' ל"ג כתב דהיכא שהמרש' והמורש' הם עובדי כוכבים או אנוסים לא מהני הרשא' בין בדיני ישראל בין בעש"ע אף לר"ת וע"ש וכתב בתשו' דברי ריבות סימן ש"א דלדעת ר"ת ה"ה דעובד כוכבים יכול להרשות לישראל ע"ש ובתשובת הרשד"ם סימן נ"ט פסק דאף ר"ת מודה דעובד כוכבים א"י להרשות ישראל וע"ש. ש"ך:
baer_hetev.en:
A non-Jew. The Sema cites the Tur that Rabbeinu Tam derives from Scripture that a non-Jew may acquire through barter. Therefore, when the non-Jew gives his cloth to the Jewish principal, the principal takes hold of it and transfers in exchange the debt or deposit that he has in another's possession, the non-Jew acquires it as an authorized representative. This works only when the non-Jew personally gives the barter object to the Jew. Witnesses cannot make the kinyan on his behalf in the usual manner, where witnesses give their own cloth to the transferor and thereby acquire for the recipient under the rule that one may acquire for another in his absence. The Tur states in siman 195 that most kinyanim in his time were made that way, and the witnesses would write that they acquired from the transferor for the recipient with a valid utensil. When the authorization is made directly to a non-Jew, however, the witnesses do not act as agents to acquire for him. They therefore write that the non-Jew himself made the barter acquisition. The Shach writes that Maharshal disagrees and concludes that for a loan or other property that cannot itself be transferred by barter, authorization to a non-Jew plainly does not work because there the representative acts only as an agent, and a non-Jew cannot serve as a halachic agent. Land or a deposit, however, can be transferred to the non-Jew by a valid kinyan sudar if barter works for a non-Jew. In that case the authorization should omit the clause binding the principal to everything litigated, because that is agency language. Responsa Maharashdam 59 writes similarly. The Shach suggests that Rabbeinu Tam may also mean only this. The Mechaber's wording, however, seems to imply that authorization to a non-Jew works in every context. The Shach remains doubtful even about the underlying premise that barter works for a non-Jew. He discusses the proofs at length and notes that Responsa Maharam Mintz 5 states simply that no barter acquisition exists for a non-Jew. Maharashdam 59 likewise says that Rabbeinu Tam's view appears to be an isolated opinion, though without giving the reason.
Agency. Responsa Rashach II, 33, writes that where both the principal and representative are non-Jews, or forced converts, authorization is ineffective under either Jewish law or their civil law even according to Rabbeinu Tam. Responsa Divrei Rivot 301 writes that according to Rabbeinu Tam a non-Jew may authorize a Jew. Maharashdam 59 rules that even Rabbeinu Tam agrees that a non-Jew cannot appoint a Jew as authorized representative. Shach.

beer_hagolah.he: שם סעיף ט"ו בשם ר"ת וכ"כ התוס' בשמו בריש קידושין דף ג' סוף ע"א ומבואר טעמו שם
beer_hagolah.en: There, seif 15, in the name of Rabbeinu Tam. Tosafot likewise write in his name at the beginning of Kiddushin 3a, and the reason is explained there.

beur_hagra.he:
יכולים כו'. דעכו"ם קונה בקנין כמ"ש בקדושין ג' סד"א אמינא כו' ושם ח' א' ואידך ה"ק בתורת כסף כו':
דאין כו'. ב"מ ע"א ע"ב רבינא כו' ולא היא כו'. ומ"מ יכול להרשות אע"ג דק"ל שליח שויה היינו שלא יוכל לעכבם. מרדכי פ' מרובה:
beur_hagra.en:
They can, etc. A non-Jew can acquire through a kinyan, as stated in Kiddushin 3 and there 8a, "I might have thought," etc., and according to the other view, "This is what it means: by means of money," etc.
For there is no, etc. See Bava Metzia 71b to 72a, the discussion of Ravina, etc., "but that is not so," etc. Nevertheless, one may appoint him by formal authorization. Although we hold that such a person is merely an agent, that means only that the representative may not retain the property for himself. Mordechai, chapter Merubah.

chelkat_mechokek.he: לאחר שהתפללו הקהל ערבית. וכתב בסדר הגט של מהר"י מינץ סימן ע' ראיתי שהחמיר מהר"מ וסבירא ליה אפילו אחר תפלה של הקהל אף על גב דאיהו לא התפלל בב"ה שלו והיה עוד היום גדול החמיר שלא ליתן גט, תשובת מהר"י מולין ז"ל עכ"ל והב"י לקמן סימן קל"ו כתב ואיני יודע מה ענין דין לגט ושום א' מהפוסקים לא חילק בכך וכן פסק הב"י לקמן סימן קנ"ד שבשעת הדחק אפילו בלילה ממש יכתוב וינתן:
chelkat_mechokek.en: After the congregation has prayed Ma'ariv. In the get procedure of Mahari Mintz, siman 70, he writes: "I saw Maharam act stringently. Even after the congregation had prayed, although he himself had not yet prayed Ma'ariv in his synagogue and it was still broad daylight, he was stringent not to deliver a get." This is from Responsa Maharil. Beit Yosef, however, writes below in siman 136: "I do not know what connection adjudication has to a get, and none of the authorities made such a distinction." Beit Yosef also rules below in siman 154 that in pressing circumstances one may even write and deliver a get at actual nighttime.

ketzot_hachoshen.he:
["שיזהר מלכתוב ז\"ל הט\"ז לפי' הסמ\"ע דבסודר תלי' מלתא של מי יהי' הי' להפוסקים להזכיר ענין הסודר ולא הכתיב' וכ\"ת דהא בהא תליא דאם הסודר של העדים דוקא כתבינן וקנינא הא ליתי' דהא בימי התלמוד הי' הקונ' נותן הסודר ואפ\"ה היו כותבין ל' קנינא כדאי' פ' י\"נ אלא נלענ\"ד דיכולים העדים לתת סודר שלהם לכותי להקנות לו רק שלא יכתוב בלשון השטר וקנינא מיני' דהלשון מורה על שליחות שקנו בשבילו דאין שליחות לכותי אלא שיכתבו וקנה הכותי דהיינו ע\"י הסודר של העדים שעל ידו קונה חוב פ' עכ\"ל והגאון ח\"צ כתב עליו ז\"ל אמר המגיה דברי הרב שגבו ממני עכ\"ל: אמנם דע לכאורה יראה דסודר שנותנין העדים אינו אלא בתורת שליחות אבל כתבנו בסי' קצ\"ה סק\"ט דע\"כ אינו משום שליחות מדכתב בש\"ע שם אין קונין בשבת ואם קנו אעפ\"י שעשו עבירה קנו ואע\"ג דכבר הי' מנהג בזמניהם שעדים נותנין סודר שלהם וכמ\"ש בטור בשם הרא\"ש וא\"כ אין שליח לדבר עבירה ואפי' במידי דרבנן ולכן העליתי שמה דאין צריך שליחות אלא כיון שנותנין סודר שלהם קנה מדין עבד כנעני וכדאמרינן פ\"ק דקידושין דף ח' הילך מנה ויהי' שדך מכור לפ' דקנה אותו פ' מדין עבד כנעני ובעבד כנעני אמרינן פ\"ק דקידושין דאפי' בע\"כ של העבד הוא משום דקבלת רבו גרמה ואע\"ג דקנין אינו בע\"כ מ\"מ כל שהוא רוצה אינו צריך שליחות וקנה ממילא ע\"י סודר של העדים וע\"ש באורך וא\"כ ה\"נ מהני אפי' בעכו\"ם כיון דאינו צריך שליחות וממילא קנה ע\"י סודר של אחרים וקבלת מקנה גורם ולזה העיקר שלא לכתוב בלשון המורה שליחות אלא שיכתבו וקנה הכותי והוא קונה ע\"י סודר של העדים וז\"ב) (וכן משמע מדברי תוס' ישנים פ\"ק דקידושין וז\"ל שלא לכתוב וקנינא מיניה דקנינא מיניה משמע שהעדים שלוחים לקבל הקנין ואין שליחות כו' ומשמע דאין הקפידא רק על כתיבה שלא לכתוב בלשון שליחות ודוק:"]
["וקנה העכו\"ם מדין חליפין בא\"י עיין ש\"ך ובתומים כתב ז\"ל והנה מכאן נראה דקנין אגב אינו בכותי דאל\"כ למה לא ציוה ר\"ת בהרשא' של כותי לכתוב אג\"ק וגם בחמץ ובכורות למה לא ציוו המחברים להקנות אג\"ק כמו שבאמת לא מצינו בשום דוכתא דקנין אג\"ק יועיל בכותי ע\"ש וכתבו אגב ריהטא דהא כבר כתוב קנין אגב בדברי ר' ירוחם נתיב ך' ח\"ב ז\"ל ולצאת ידי שניהם יקבל מהכותי מעות בשביל אזן הבהמה כו' או יקנה להכותי המקום שבהמה עומדת שם ויקנה לו אגבי' אזן הבהמה מן העובר וע\"ש וכבר נתפשט בכל ישראל במכירת חמץ על קנין אג\"ק והוא מדברי הגאון מוהר\"ש קודנייבור דשדי נרגא בקנין חצר משום דחצר מדין שליחות ואין שליחות לכותי וז\"ב:"]
ketzot_hachoshen.en:
He must be careful how he writes it. Taz writes that according to Sema's explanation, if the effectiveness of the kinyan depends on whose sudar is used, the decisors should have discussed the sudar rather than the wording of the document. One might answer that the two depend on each other: if specifically the witnesses' sudar is used, one writes, "and we effected a kinyan." But this cannot be right, because in Talmudic times the purchaser himself commonly supplied the sudar and nevertheless documents were written with the language, "and we effected a kinyan," as stated in Perek Yesh Nochalin. It therefore appears to Taz that the witnesses may give their own sudar to a gentile so that he acquires through it. They must only avoid writing, "and we effected a kinyan from him," because that wording implies that the witnesses acted as his agents in accepting the kinyan, and there is no halachic agency for a gentile. Rather, they should write that the gentile acquired, meaning that he acquired through the witnesses' sudar. Chacham Tzvi commented upon these words, "The rabbi's words have overcome me." However, at first glance one might think that when the witnesses give their own sudar, they act only as agents. Yet in siman 195, seif katan 9, I proved that this cannot be the reason. The Shulchan Aruch there says one does not effect a kinyan on Shabbat, but if they did so, although they committed a prohibition, the kinyan is valid. Already in their time it was customary for the witnesses to give their own sudar, as the Tur cites from the Rosh. If their act depended upon agency, there would be no agency for a transgression, even for a rabbinic prohibition. I therefore concluded there that agency is unnecessary. Once the witnesses give their sudar, the recipient acquires under the principle learned from a Canaanite slave. Kiddushin teaches: if one says, "Here is a maneh, and let your field be sold to so and so," that third person acquires through the law of the Canaanite slave. In the law of a Canaanite slave, the acquisition can operate even without the slave's will, because the master's receipt effects the change. Although an ordinary acquisition cannot be forced upon someone against his will, where the recipient wants the acquisition no agency is required. He acquires automatically through the sudar supplied by the witnesses and through the transferor's receipt. The same therefore works with a gentile, because agency is not needed. The essential point is only that the document not use language implying agency. It should say that the gentile acquired, for he acquires through the witnesses' sudar. This is clear. Old Tosafot in the first chapter of Kiddushin implies the same. They write that one should not write, "and we effected a kinyan from him," because that wording implies that the witnesses are agents to receive the kinyan, and there is no agency for a gentile. The concern is therefore only with writing a formulation of agency.
And the gentile acquires through barter in Eretz Yisrael. See the Shach. Tumim writes that this passage appears to show that acquisition incidentally with land does not work for a gentile. Otherwise, he asks, why did Rabbeinu Tam not instruct that an authorization written for a gentile should use acquisition incidentally with land? Likewise, in the laws of chametz and firstborn animals, why did the decisors not instruct that the property be transferred incidentally with land? He concludes that nowhere do we find acquisition incidentally with land functioning for a gentile. These words were written too hastily. Rabbeinu Yerucham already states expressly, in Netiv 20, part 2, that to satisfy all opinions one should receive money from the gentile for the animal's ear, or transfer to the gentile the place where the animal stands and transfer the ear of the fetus to him incidentally with that land. Thus acquisition incidentally with land is explicitly stated regarding a gentile. Indeed, this method has become widespread throughout Israel in the sale of chametz. It follows the ruling of the Gaon Rabbi Shmuel of Koidanov, who questioned acquisition through a courtyard because a courtyard functions through agency, and there is no agency for a gentile. The practice therefore relied upon acquisition incidentally with land. This is clear.

meirat_einayim.he: יכולין לשלוח הרשאה ביד עכו"ם. עיין בטור דשם כ' דילפינן מקרא דהעכו"ם קונה בחליפין מ"ה ג"כ כשעכו"ם נותן לו סודרו להישראל המרשה ואוחז בו ומקנה לו חליפיו חובו או פקדונו שיש לו ביד אחר זכה העכו"ם בו כדין מורשה ומהני. מיהו זה דוקא כשהעכו"ם עצמו מוסר החליפין לישראל וקונה ע"י ממנו תביעת ממון שמרשה לו עליו אבל אין עדים יכולין לקנות עבורו מהמרשה כדרך שאר קנינים דהעדים נותנין סודר שלהם להמקנ' והם זוכים להקונה עבורו כי זוכין לאדם שלא בפניו (וכמ"ש הטור בשם הרא"ש לקמן בסי' קצ"ה שכן היו רוב הקנינים גם בזמניהם כיון דמדרך העולם ליקח עדים להקנייה כדי שלא יבא הכחשה ביניהם ואגב שמיחדים עדים לזה נוהגין ג"כ העדי' לעשות הקנין בסודר שלהם דהזוכה) ואז כותבין העדים קנינו מפלוני המקנה לפלוני הזוכה במנא דכשר למקניא ביה (וכמו שאנו נוהגין דכותבין כן בשטרותינו) וזהו שסיים בטור וכתב דבהקנה להעכו"ם ע"י אין כותבין בהרשאה וקנינא מיניה (דהוי משמע דהקנה המרשה להעכו"ם ע"י העדים) דהא אין העדים נעשים שלוחים לזכות להעכו"ם ע"י אלא יכתוב וקנה העכו"ם ור"ל שהעכו"ם באמת עושה הקנין חליפין בעצמו ויכתבו העדים כן בהרשאה שקנה העכו"ם וק"ל זהו נ"ל פשוט בדברי הט"ו בענין זה דכתבו שיזהר מלכתוב וקנינא מיניה כו' ולא כע"ש שכתב בזה ז"ל ובלבד שיזהר מלכתוב ביה וקנינא מיני' שמשמע שהעכו"ם הקנה דבר לאחר וקי"ל דאין שליחות לעכו"ם שאינו יכול לזכות משלו לאחרים אלא יכתוב וקנה העכו"ם כלומר שהוא קנה מה שכתוב בהרשא' ולקנות יש לו יד עכ"ל. נרא' שלא דק לא בהענין ולא בהלשון ועפ"ר:
meirat_einayim.en: They may send an authorization through a gentile. The Tur explains that Scripture teaches that a gentile can acquire through exchange. Therefore, when the gentile himself gives his kerchief to the Jewish principal, and the principal takes it and transfers in exchange the debt or deposit he has against another person, the gentile acquires the claim with the status of an authorized representative. This works only where the gentile personally supplies the object used for the exchange and thereby acquires the monetary claim. Witnesses cannot make the acquisition on his behalf in the usual manner, where the witnesses give their own kerchief to the transferor and acquire on behalf of the recipient under the rule that one may acquire a benefit for a person in his absence. The Tur writes in the name of the Rosh in siman 195 that most acquisitions were already conducted in that manner in their time, because parties normally summon witnesses to avoid later denial, and once witnesses are designated they also conduct the kinyan with their own kerchief on behalf of the recipient. The witnesses then write that they acquired from the transferor on behalf of the recipient with a utensil fit for acquisition, as is customary in our documents. Therefore the Tur concludes that where the claim is transferred to a gentile in this manner, the authorization should not say, 'and we acquired from him,' because that would imply that the witnesses acquired from the principal on behalf of the gentile, and witnesses cannot serve as agents to acquire for a gentile in that way. Rather, the document should state that 'the gentile acquired,' meaning that the gentile personally performed the exchange acquisition, and the witnesses attest to that fact. This appears to me the straightforward meaning of the Tur and Mechaber's warning not to write, 'and we acquired from him.' The Ir Shushan explains that phrase differently, as though it implied that the gentile transferred something to another person and that the problem is that a gentile cannot appoint an agent to acquire for someone else. He therefore says to write instead that the gentile acquired what is stated in the authorization. In my view, he was not precise either in the legal concept or in the wording.

netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.he: יכתוב וקנה העכו"ם. ר"ל שעשה העכו"ם הקנין בעצמו ולא בסודר של העדים דאין שליחות לעכו"ם והש"ך מסופק אי מהני קנין חליפין בעכו"ם:
netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.en: He shall write, and the gentile acquired. Meaning, the gentile himself performed the act of acquisition and did not acquire through the witnesses' scarf, because a gentile cannot act through halachic agency. The Shach remains uncertain whether barter acquisition is effective with a gentile.

pitchei_teshuva.he: ביד עכו"ם. עבה"ט ביד אך לבי מהסס בעיקר הדין שסובר ר"ת דחליפין מועיל בעכו"ם כו' ועיין בתומים שהאריך לסתור דברי הש"ך בזה ובסוף כתב ומכאן נרא' דקנין אגב אינו בעכו"ם דאל"כ למה לא צוה ר"ת בהרשא' של עכו"ם לכתוב אג"ק וגם בחמץ ובכורות למה לא ציוו המחברים להקנות אג"ק כמו שבאמת לא מצינו בשום דוכתא דקנין אגב קרקע יועיל בעכו"ם ע"ש ובס' קצה"ח השיג עליו וכ' דאגב ריהטא כתב כן דהא כבר כתוב קנין אגב בדברי רבינו ירוחם נתיב ך' ח"ב כו' וכבר נתפשט בכל ישראל במכירה חמץ על קנין אג"ק והוא מדברי הגאון מהרש"ק (בת' שבספר נחלת שבעה ח"ב סי' ל' והביאו ג"כ הח"י בסי' תמ"ח סקי"ד ע"ש) דשדי נרגא בקנין חצר משום דחצר מדין שליחות ואין שליחות לעכו"ם וזה ביאורו ע"ש ועיין בת' חתם סופר חח"מ סימן ס"ו שכתוב שנמצא כן להדיא כדברי הקצה"ח הנכתב לעיל בל' הנ"ל בל' הרמב"ן במלחמות פ"ב דפסחים בסוגיא דהרהונו אצלו ע"ש עוד:
pitchei_teshuva.en: In the possession of a non Jew. See Baer Heitev through its expression of doubt about Rabbeinu Tam's view that exchange acquisition is effective with a non Jew. The Tumim argues at length against the Shach and concludes that acquisition by means of land does not operate with a non Jew. Otherwise, why did Rabbeinu Tam not instruct that an authorization against a non Jew be made by acquisition together with land? Likewise, in the sale of chametz and firstborn animals, the halachic authorities did not originally direct use of acquisition together with land. He maintains that no source clearly establishes that such an acquisition works with a non Jew. Ketzot HaChoshen challenges him and writes that this was stated too hastily, since Rabbeinu Yerucham, Netiv 20, part 2, expressly mentions acquisition together with land. Moreover, the Jewish communities had already widely adopted acquisition together with land in the sale of chametz, following the responsum of Maharash Kaidanover printed in Nachalat Shivah, part 2, siman 30, and cited by Chok Yaakov, siman 448, seif katan 14. Maharash Kaidanover questioned acquisition by courtyard because a courtyard acquires by the law of agency, and there is no agency for a non Jew, and therefore preferred acquisition together with land. Ketzot explains the matter there. Responsa Chatam Sofer, Choshen Mishpat, siman 66, writes that an explicit source supporting Ketzot is found in Ramban's Milchamot to the second chapter of Pesachim, in the discussion of one who pledged chametz with the creditor. See there further.

siftei_kohen.he:
[" יכולים לשלוח הרשאה ע\"י עכו\"ם כו'. ומהרש\"ל שם סי' ס\"ג חולק אזה והעלה דבהלואה ושאר דברים שאינן נקנים בחליפין פשיטא שאין הרשאה מועיל לעכו\"ם דכיון דלא יוכל לעשות מורש' בכה\"ג אלא מטעם שליחות וכמו שנתבאר לעיל ואין שליחות לעכו\"ם אבל בקרקע ופקדון יכול להקנות לעכו\"ם בק\"ס שמועיל חליפים לעכו\"ם אבל לא יכתוב כל מה דמתעני עליה מן דינא שהוא לשון שליחות כו' עכ\"ד (וכה\"ג כ' בתשובת מהרשד\"ם סי' נ\"ט ע\"ש) ובזה היה נראה לומר דגם דעת ר\"ת כן שאינו יכול לעשות הרשאה אלא בדבר שנקנה בחליפין והיינו דהטור וסמ\"ג ומרדכי שהביאו דברי ר\"ת כולם הביאו טעמו בצדו דילפינן מכסף מקנתו שמועיל חליפים בעכו\"ם ונרא' לדעתם דאף שכתב בהרשאה כל מה דמתעני מ\"מ כיון שהוא בענין שנקנ' בחליפי' אמרי' דהעכו\"ם קונה קנין גמור ומ\"ש כל מה דמתעני הוא כמו שמקבל עליו אחריות ולא שיעשה העכו\"ם שליח. רק מדברי המחבר משמע דהרשאה מועיל בעכו\"ם בכל ענין. אך לבי מהסס בעיקר הדין שסובר ר\"ת דחליפים מועיל לעכו\"ם דלא אישתמיט בשום מקום בש\"ס דעכו\"ם קונה בחליפים וכן בפוסקים לא אישתמיט חד מנייהו שהזכיר דין זה במקומות שהזכירו דיני קנין לעכו\"ם. וכן בש\"ס פרק בתרא דעכו\"ם (דף ע\"א) אמר רב להני סבוית' כי כייליתו חמר' לעכו\"ם שקלי זוזי מנייהו והדר כיילי להו ואי לא נקיטי בהדייהו זוזי אוזפינהו והדר שקלינהו מנייהו כי היכא דתיהוי הלוא' גבייהו דאי לא עבדיתו הכי כי קא הוי י\"נ ברשותייכו קא הוי וכי קא שקליתו דמייין נסך קשקליתו. ואם איתא הל\"ל אקנינהו ניהליהו בחליפים ואע\"ג דמשמע התם דלמ\"ד משיכ' מועיל בעכו\"ם ה\"ה דהוי מהני משיכה היינו משום דזימנין דאיכא עכבת יין אפומי דכונתא דקמא קמא אינסך ליה וכדאיתא בש\"ס שם אבל תקנתא דחליפין מועיל בכל גוני ואפשר לא היו רגילי' להקנות לעכו\"ם בחליפין וגם גבי בכור האריכו כל הפוסקים למצוא היתר להקנות הבהמה לעכו\"ם משום דמספקא להו אי קי\"ל כר\"ל או כר' יוחנן דפליגי אי משיכה או מעות קונה בעכו\"ם וכמו שנתבאר בי\"ד סי' ש\"ך ואם איתא הל\"ל דיקנה לעכו\"ם בחליפין וכן גבי חמץ האריכו הפוסקים וכל האחרונים לעשות בהיתר להקנות לו היכא דלא אפשר במשיכה ואם איתא לקנינהו ניהלי' בחליפים והראי' שהביא ר\"ת מכסף מקנתו אף שאיני כדאי להשיב על דברי ר\"ת מ\"מ תורה היא ואענ' חלקי. שלפע\"ד לאו ראי' היא דלעול' אימא לך חליפים אינו מועיל בעכו\"ם והא דממעטינן מכסף מקנתו דלא נקנה בחליפים היינו דאפילו לישראל אין נקנה ע\"ע בחליפין דודאי אע\"ג דהאי קרא דמכסף מקנתו בעכו\"ם כתיב מ\"מ בישראל נמי משתעי קרא ותדע דאל\"כ הא דמשמע מכל הפוסקי' דאין ע\"ע נקנה בחליפין מנ\"ל הא אלא ודאי כדפירשתי ועוד די\"ל דקרא לגופי' אתי לגלויי' דע\"ע אין נקנה בחליפים לעכו\"ם מטעם שאין חליפים מועיל לעכו\"ם ותדע דהא רב יוסף קמפרש התם (בקידושין דף ח' ע\"א) דמכסף מקנתו ולא בתורת תבוא' וכלים טעמי' משום דלא קיץ אף ע\"ג דס\"ל לרב יוסף התם דכל שאר דברים בעולם אין מועיל קנין במידי דלא קיץ כדמוכח התם מקידושי אשה ופדיון בכור וא\"כ אמאי אצטריך קרא למעוטי ע\"ע אלא ודאי כדפירשתי גם מה שהקשה התוס' בקידושין דף ג' סוף ע\"א וז\"ל וא\"ת והיכא ס\"ד דנילף משדה עפרון שתקנה אשה בחליפין והא שדה עפרון גופא לא מיקני בחליפין דלא מצינו חליפי' לעכו\"ם דהא אמרי' בבכורות מדישראל בחדא עכו\"ם נמי בחדא וי\"ל דהיינו לבר מחליפי' כו' וכן משמע לקמן גבי נמכר לעכו\"ם מכסף מקנתו כו' עכ\"ל נלפע\"ד העיקר כמו שהבינו בקושיית' דאין חליפי' לעכו\"ם ואפ\"ה הוי ס\"ד דאש' תקנ' בחליפי' כמו שדה דאע\"ג דעפרון עכו\"ם הוה מ\"מ שדה עצמה נקנית בחליפין לישראל וה\"א דה\"ה אשה (וכן מצאתי בתשו' מהר\"ם מינץ סי' ה' דף י\"ב ע\"א שכתב בפשיטות דלא מצינו חליפין לעכו\"ם דוקא כסף או משיכ' הוי קניית עכו\"ם למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה ע\"כ שוב מצאתי בתשו' מהרשד\"ם סי' נ\"ט שכ' שנלפע\"ד שסברת ר\"ת דעת יחיד היא כו' אך שלא כתב טעם לדבר וע\"ש):"]
[" ובלבד שיזהר כו'. דקנינא משמע שהעדים קנו מהישראל ושוב נעשו (ועיין בתשובת ר\"ש כהן ספר ב' סי' ל\"ג כתב דהיכא שהמרש' והמורש' הם עכו\"ם או אנוסים ל\"מ הרשאה בין בדיני ישראל בין בעש\"ע אף לר\"ת וע\"ש) שלוחים לזכות לעכו\"ם ואין זכיי' לעכו\"ם אלא יכתוב וקנה העכו\"ם והיינו שקנה העכו\"ם עצמו בחליפין (וכתב בתשו' דברי ריבות סי' ש\"א דלדעת ר\"ת ה\"ה דעכו\"ם יכול להרשות לישראל ע\"ש ובתשובת ר\"ש מדינ' סי' נ\"ט פסק דאף ר\"ת מודה דעכו\"ם א\"י להרשות ישראל ומכ\"ש שעל ישראל זה נאמר לא טוב עשה (עכו\"ם) [צ\"ל בעמיו] ע\"ש):"]
siftei_kohen.en:
They may send an authorization through a non-Jew. Maharshal disputes this. For a loan or anything else not transferable by symbolic exchange, authorization cannot be given to a non-Jew, because it operates only as agency and a non-Jew cannot serve as a halachic agent. Land or a deposit, however, can be transferred to a non-Jew by symbolic exchange, though the authorization should not use language of agency. This may also be Rabbeinu Tam's intent, since the authorities who cite him immediately give his reason that symbolic exchange is effective for a non-Jew. On that view, even if the document uses the customary formula, the non-Jew acquires fully and the additional language merely imposes responsibility. Mechaber, however, implies that authorization is effective through a non-Jew in every case. I remain doubtful of Rabbeinu Tam's basic premise that symbolic exchange acquires for a non-Jew. Neither the Gemara nor the authorities discussing acquisition by non-Jews commonly mention it. The Gemara concerning wine sold to non-Jews could simply have advised acquisition by symbolic exchange, yet it instead requires payment or another recognized mode. The authorities concerning transfer of an animal to a non-Jew to avoid firstborn sanctity, and concerning sale of chametz, likewise labor to use money or pulling and do not suggest symbolic exchange. Rabbeinu Tam's proof from “the money of his purchase” is not conclusive. The verse may teach that even a Jewish slave is not acquired by symbolic exchange, or may reveal specifically that a Hebrew slave sold to a non-Jew is not acquired by that method because symbolic exchange is ineffective for a non-Jew. Tosafot's question in Kiddushin is better understood according to its initial assumption that symbolic exchange does not work for a non-Jew. A woman might still have been compared to a field because a field itself is acquired by symbolic exchange when both parties are Jews, even though Ephron personally was a non-Jew. Maharam Mintz and Maharshdam also write that no acquisition by symbolic exchange is found for a non-Jew. Rabbeinu Tam's view therefore appears to be an individual opinion.

urim_vetumim_tumim.he: אלא שכ"ז שהמורשה אלם וכו' הרב הש"ך בס"ק ל"ב השיג על רמ"א בכוונת התוספות ומפרש מ"ש התוספות שהוא אלם היינו הנתבע אלם ולכך התובע נמנע לילך עמו ומעמיד להמורשה במקומו ומלבד דדין זה ליתא דאדרבא בזה יפה עושה מורשה דאינו גר מפני איש ואם זה התובע יש לו מורך לבב ונפסד עי"כ והוא המורשה אוזר חיילם לקום נגדו ולא יחת מפני איש וכושל יקימון מילו אני אומר תבוא עליו ברכה וכמה שקדו חז"ל לשבר מתלעות האלמים וזרוע רמה עד שהכריחו להביא עדות מה שכנגדו ואיך לא נשקוד שהמורשה יקום בחריקאו של איש נעזב. אף גם הא מבואר בפסקי תוספות למסכת שבועות להדיא אלם ובעל טענות לא יתעבר לטעון בשביל חבירו עד כאן והדבר מבואר כמ"ש הרמ"א ובעיקר קושיתו דמה יהיה באלמתו וטענותיו הא אסור לו לטעון שקר לק"מ כי חדא לרב טענותיו יתרצה הנתבע ע"כ לפשר דבר כי יהיה נלאה נשוא דברי ריבות שלו וטרחא דבית דין וגם העדים אפשר דיגורו ממנו כעובדא דמרי בר איסק. ועיין ת"ה סימן ש"ו ויש"ש לב"ק פרק ד' דין י"ח אם יכול אדם להרבות בתואנה ועלילות כדי לכוף חבירו לפשר ועיין שם דבטענה שיש בו ממש מותר ודברי רמ"א פה עיקר:
urim_vetumim_tumim.en: Except that whenever the authorized agent is forceful, etc. The Shach in seif katan 32 challenges the Rama's understanding of Tosafot and explains that when Tosafot speak of an "overbearing" person they mean that the defendant is overbearing. The claimant is therefore afraid to litigate with him personally and appoints an authorized agent instead. Apart from the fact that the Shach's resulting law is incorrect, for in such a case the agent acts properly by not fearing any man, and if the claimant is fainthearted and would otherwise lose his rights while the agent girds himself with strength to stand against the overbearing defendant and not be intimidated, he should be blessed for supporting one who would stumble. Our Sages labored greatly to break the teeth and power of violent men, even compelling such a person to bring the evidence held by his opponent. How then could we object when an authorized agent stands in the place of one who has been abandoned and intimidated? Moreover, Piskei Tosafot to Shevuot expressly state: "An overbearing and argumentative person should not intrude to argue on behalf of his fellow." This plainly means, as the Rama understood, that the authorized agent himself is overbearing and excessively argumentative. As for the Shach's main question, what harm could arise merely from the agent's forcefulness and arguments if he is forbidden to argue falsely, there is no difficulty. Through his many arguments the defendant may agree to a compromise because he grows weary of the contentious proceedings and the burden imposed on beit din. Witnesses too may fear him, as in the incident of Mari bar Isak. See Terumat HaDeshen siman 306 and Maharshal, Bava Kamma chapter 4, law 18, concerning whether one may employ numerous procedural claims and pressures to force another to compromise. See there that where the contentions have substance, it is permitted. The Rama's ruling here is therefore primary.

עשה. (ומיהו הבא בהרשא' כדי ליהנות מן השכר לא בשביל אלמות נראה דאינו בכלל ואשר לא טוב עשה בעמיו. ג"ת דף ש' וכן פשט המנהג. כנה"ג):
אלם. נרא' דהרמ"א הבין מ"ש הב"י בשם התוס' דר"ל שהמורש' הוא אלם אבל זה אינו אלא כוונת התוס' לומר דלפעמים המלו' אינו רוצה לדון עם הלו' מחמת שהלו' הוא אלם ובעל טענות ואינו רוצה לריב עמו א"כ מורש' זה לא טוב עושה שמתעבר על ריב לא לו ומה לו בזה יתבענו המלוה בעצמו אבל כשאין יכול לטרוח להביא מעותיו מצוה קעביד וכ"מ בכ"מ דכונת התוס' שהלוה הוא אלם ולפ"ז נראה דאין כאן פלוגת' כלל וכולם לדבר אחד נתכוונו דכל שהמורש' עושה מחמת שהוא בענין שאין המרש' יכול לעשות כן מצוה קעביד. רק כשהם בעיר א' והמרש' יכול לעשות כמו המורש' רק שמונע מפני אלמות הלוה א"כ מתעבר כו'. ש"ך:

Do. (From his next wife in Harsh to enjoy the wages, not for Almas, Dao seems to have done so at his people. A page , and a custom. honest:
A forceful person. Rama appears to have understood Beit Yosef's citation of Tosafot as referring to a forceful representative. This is not the intent. Tosafot mean that sometimes a creditor does not wish to litigate with a debtor because the debtor is forceful and skilled in contentious argument, and the creditor does not want to quarrel with him. In such a case, a representative who inserts himself into the dispute is not acting properly, because he is involving himself in a quarrel that is not his own. The creditor can pursue his claim personally. If, however, the creditor is unable to undertake the trouble of collecting his money, the representative performs a mitzvah by assisting him. This also appears from Kesef Mishneh, which understands Tosafot as referring to a forceful debtor. According to this, there is no dispute at all. Everyone agrees that when the representative acts because the principal is genuinely unable to do what must be done, he performs a mitzvah. Only when they are in the same city and the principal could do exactly what the representative does, but refrains merely because of the debtor's forcefulness, is the representative considered one who involves himself in another's quarrel. Shach.
In his presence. Meaning, not in the presence of the person for whom he is acting as attorney. The witnesses cannot acquire on his behalf without his knowledge in a matter that may be detrimental to him, for this is called one who has done what is not good. Therefore, even if he later consents, it is of no effect, since the acquisition did not take effect initially. This is the view of Rivak in Mordechai. Although he cites the view of Ri that where the principal cannot trouble himself the agent performs a mitzvah and this is not detrimental, Rama nevertheless rules in accordance with Rivak, whose reasoning is persuasive: even if he performs a mitzvah, most people do not consent to involve themselves in a quarrel that is not theirs, and at times the verse, one who has done what is not good, is applied to such a person. Therefore, even if he later consents, we do not say that the matter is revealed retroactively; his consent is effective only from then onward, and the acquisition did not initially take effect. This is the Sema. Shach objects that Rama too speaks only of the case explained earlier, such as where the opposing party is violent or the like; where the agent performs a mitzvah, however, one may certainly appoint an attorney for another even without his presence. See there. Taz likewise rules against the Sema; see there.

הרי זה עושה מצוה. ☜ וכתב המרדכי פרק המפקיד דהמורש' אסור לטעון שקר ואפי' הבעל דבר בעצמו אסור לשקר (וע"ל סי' י"ב ס"ו) והא דאפוטרופוס מותר משו' דאם הי' אביהם קיים הי' טוען כן ד"מ סי' קכ"ד:
שלא בפניו פי' שלא בפני המורשה שלא יקנה המרש' בפני עדים בקנין סודר שלא בפני המורש' דאמר הריני מקנה ומרשה לפלוני על חובי להוציאו מיד פלוני דאין העדים קונין לו שלא מדעת דבר כזה שיש לו בו חובה שהרי אמרי' להמורש' אשר לא טוב עשה ולכן אפי' אם נתרצה אחר כך אינו כלום כיון דהקנין לא חל מעיקרא ☜ וע"ש במרדכי פרק מרובה דכתב כן תחל' בשם ר' יודא בר קלונימוס וכ' עליו ז"ל אמנם לפמ"ש ר"י ניחא דפי' דההיא איירי דוקא כשהוא עושה שליח בשביל שהוא אלם ובעל טענות אבל כשהוא טורח להביא מעותיו לחבירו שאין חבירו יכול לטרוח אין זה חובה ואדרב' מצוה קעביד להציל עשוק מיד עושקו עכ"ל וצריכין ליתן טעם לדברי מור"ם למה השמיט מסקנת המרדכי דנדא' ממנו דס"ל דלכל הפחות אם נתרצ' אח"כ דשרי ובע"ש כתב מסקנא זו לחוד דכתב ולכן אם נתרצ' אח"כ בדבר וקבלו קנא' שגיל' דעתו למפרע עכ"ל. ונרא' דדעת מור"ם הכריע כדברי ר"י בר קלונימוס דמסתבר טעמי' משום דאף אם מצו' קעביד מ"מ על הרוב אין אדם מתרצ' להיות מורש' ולהכניס ראשו בריב לא לו ולפעמים קוראין עליו ואשר לא טוב עשה מ"ה ס"ל דאף אם נתרצ' אח"כ אין אומרים דאיגלאי מלתא למפרע כיון דאין דרך העולם להתרצות בזה ואין לנו אלא מהריצוי ואילך לא למפרע ומתחל' לא חל הקנין ודלא כע"ש:
meirat_einayim.en:
He thereby performs a mitzvah. Mordechai writes that an authorized representative may not plead falsely. Even the litigant himself may not lie. A guardian is permitted to advance claims that the deceased father could have made, because that is part of protecting the orphan's rights.
Not in his presence. Meaning the principal should not effect a kinyan authorizing another person outside that person's presence, saying before witnesses, "I transfer and authorize so-and-so over my claim against so-and-so." Witnesses cannot acquire for a person without his knowledge something that may be a burden to him. The Gemara's expression regarding a representative, "he did what is not good," reflects that serving as representative can be an unwanted burden. Therefore, even if he later agrees, the original kinyan may not have taken effect. Mordechai first writes this in the name of Rabbi Yehudah bar Kalonymus. He then cites Rabbeinu Yitzchak, who distinguishes: the criticism applies when someone appoints a representative merely because that representative is forceful and skilled in claims, whereas one who undertakes the burden in order to recover another's money when the owner cannot trouble himself is performing a mitzvah by rescuing the oppressed from the oppressor. According to that approach, later consent may perhaps validate the authorization. Levush rules only according to this latter conclusion and says later acceptance reveals consent retroactively. Rama, however, appears to follow Rabbi Yehudah bar Kalonymus. Even if representation can be a mitzvah, most people do not want to insert themselves into another person's dispute, and sometimes the verse "he did what is not good" truly applies. Therefore later consent does not retroactively create a kinyan that never initially took effect; it works only from the time of consent onward.

[" וי\"א כו'. לפע\"ד דברי הרב מגומגמים וגם מ\"ש שכל זמן שהמורשה הוא אלם כו' נ' שהבין מ\"ש הב\"י בשם התוס' דה\"מ כשהוא אלם ובעל טענות שמתעבר על ריב לא לו ר\"ל שהמורש' אלם ולפע\"ד זה אינו דממ\"נ אם יטעון המורשה אמת מה בכך שהוא אלם ובעל טענות ואם מתוך שהוא אלם ובעל טענות יטעון שקר או יזכה שלא כדין ל\"ל דמתעבר על ריב לא לו תיפוק ליה דפשיטא דאסור למורשה לטעון שקר וגם אינו תלוי במורשה דפשיטא דאפי' בע\"ד בעצמו אסור לטעון שקר וכמ\"ש המרדכי בפ' המפקיד תשו' מהר\"מ וששאלתם אם האנטלר יכול לטעון כל מה שיכול לטעון להערים אפי' בדבר שיודע שאינו לא כי חלילה מעשות כן להיות חוטא ולא לו ואפי' לעצמו אינו רשאי לשקר כו' והוא פשוט אלא כוונת התוספות לומר דלפעמים המלוה אינו רוצה לדון עם הלוה מחמת שהלוה הוא אלם ובעל טענות ואינו רוצה לריב עמו א\"כ זהו שהוא מורש' לא טוב עושה שמתעבר על ריב לא לו ומה לו בזה יתבענו המלוה עצמו אבל כשטורח להביא לחברו מעותיו שאין חברו יכול לטרוח מצוה קעביד שהרי אין חברו יכול לטרוח כמו הוא וכן משמע ל' התוס' שם שכתבו זה הבא בהרשאה כשהוא עושה בשביל שהוא אלם ובעל טענות כו' וכן משמע בכסף משנה דכוונת התוס' שהלוה הוא אלם ע\"ש ולפ\"ז נראה דהראב\"ד וטור ומחבר לא פליגי עם התוס' דאדרבה כוונתם אחד דכל שהמורשה עושה מחמת שהוא בענין שאין המרש' היה יכול לעשות כן כגון שטורח הוא לו להמרשה ולא להמורשה או כגון שהמרשה הוא בעיר אחרת וכה\"ג מצוה קעביד רק כשהוא בעיר א' והמרשה יכול לעשות כמו המורשה ומה שאינו עושה כן בע\"כ הוא מפני שהלוה הוא אלם ובעל טענות א\"כ מתעבר על ריב לא לו. וגם דברי הב\"י נראין כן ע\"ש במ\"ש ולי נראה דתרוייהו איתנהו כו' ונמצא דגם מה שכתב הר\"ב וי\"א דאין חילוק כו' אינו מדוקדק. ומה שכתב בכסף משנה דתרוייהו איתנהו דכל שאינו יכול להוציא מיד הלוה מפני אלמותו או מפני ריחוק המקום מצוה קעביד כו' נראה דכוונתו שיודע שהלוה יחזיק בו שלא כדין מחמת אלמותו ולא יעיז פניו באלמותו נגד המורשה והיה מעיז נגד המרש' כגון שהמורשה הוא אדם חשוב או יודע עסקיו ועניניו ותחבוליו וכה\"ג נמצא דהוי כעין מ\"ש התוס' שטורח להביא לחברו מעותיו שאין חברו יכול לטרוח ודו\"ק:"]

siftei_kohen.en:
And some say. Rama's language is difficult. His statement that the rule applies while the agent is forceful appears to understand Tosafot as describing a forceful agent. That cannot be correct. If the agent argues truthfully, his forcefulness is irrelevant. If he lies or wins improperly, the prohibition is obvious and applies even to a litigant acting for himself. Tosafot mean that the borrower is forceful and argumentative, so the creditor avoids litigating with him. An agent who unnecessarily inserts himself into such a quarrel “intervenes in a dispute not his own.” By contrast, where he works to recover money that the creditor cannot personally pursue, he performs a mitzvah by rescuing the oppressed. Accordingly, Raavad, Tur, Mechaber, and Tosafot do not disagree. Whenever the principal cannot practically act, because of distance, burden, or similar circumstances, the agent performs a mitzvah. Where both are in the same city and the principal could act equally well, but avoids doing so only because the debtor is forceful, the agent improperly enters another's quarrel. Kesef Mishneh's statement that an agent acts meritoriously where the creditor cannot recover because of the debtor's force or distance refers to a case where the debtor would wrongfully resist the principal but not the agent, perhaps because the agent is influential or understands the debtor's tactics.
Some say that a person cannot appoint an agent. Mordechai first cites Rabbi Yehudah ben Kalonymus broadly, but then limits the rule according to Ri: where the agent merely intrudes into a quarrel because the debtor is forceful, the appointment is detrimental; where he labors to recover money the principal cannot recover, it is a mitzvah. Sema struggles to explain why Rama omitted Mordechai's conclusion and suggests that Rama rules like Rabbi Yehudah ben Kalonymus, since people generally do not wish to be drawn into others' disputes. In my view this is strained. Even Ri agrees that where accepting the agency is detrimental, it cannot be imposed without the agent's knowledge, because one may not impose a detriment upon another in his absence. Later consent does not validate the original authorization, since the acquisition never took effect. This is also the plain ruling of Shiltei HaGibborim, Ramban, and Maggid Mishneh. Rabbi Yehudah ben Kalonymus differs only in treating every such appointment as presumptively detrimental, whereas Ri allows appointment without prior knowledge where the agent's service is beneficial and meritorious. Rama's “some say” therefore concerns the detrimental case described immediately beforehand. In such a case later consent is ineffective according to all views. Ir Shushan and Sema did not state this accurately.
